newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * President Emil Constantinescu started an official visit to Japan and is due to meet Emperor Akihito and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Constantinescu meet representatives of Japan's largest corporations to discuss business opportunities in Romania.
* Reforms in Romania are genuine and are based on a good legislation, and the country's capital markets are steadily growing, Constantinescu told Japanese investors.
* The Japanese government has given Romania a $194 million loan to upgrade its infrastructure, mainly ports and roads.
* Hungary will open a consular office in Timisoara on July 23. Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin and his Hungarian opposite number Laszlo Kovacs are due to attend the ceremonies.
* The European Commission is expected to present on July 16 its report on the membership bids lodged by 10 Central and eastern European countries to join the European Union.

Romania's foreign ministry issued a statement, reacting to recent media reports the EU would invite only six states to start membership talks, saying this would contradict the EU's own principles of giving equal chances to applicants.
Romania is committed to foster efforts to meet EU membership criteria.
